summary.title: OpenCV People Counter - PyImageSearch
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a people counter in Python that counts people moving "in" and "out" of a store by combining a MobileNet SSD detector, dlib correlation tracking, and centroid tracking.
keywords: counting people entering and leaving store
takeaways: Object detectors locate objects per frame but are slow; trackers are faster and follow objects across frames, so a hybrid approach runs the detector only every N frames.
Centroid tracking matches bounding-box centers between frames by minimum Euclidean distance, registers new objects, and deregisters objects unmatched for 40 consecutive frames.
A TrackableObject stores an object ID, its centroid history, and a counted flag, which lets the script determine movement direction and avoid double counting.
The people counter uses a Caffe MobileNet SSD from OpenCV's DNN module to detect only the 'person' class, with a confidence threshold of 0.4 by default.
dlib correlation trackers follow detected people between detection passes, controlled by the --skip-frames argument (default 30).
summary.summary: The tutorial walks through building a real-time people counter that tallies people moving up or down (in or out of a department store) in a video stream or webcam feed. It explains the difference between object detection and object tracking, then describes a hybrid pipeline: a MobileNet SSD detector run every N frames, with dlib correlation trackers handling the frames in between. Centroid tracking, a lightweight algorithm that associates bounding-box centers across frames, assigns IDs and handles new or lost objects. The post then implements the project in Python with OpenCV, imutils, and dlib, covering command-line arguments, the TrackableObject class, and the main frame loop. The page text is cut off before the counting logic and results are shown.
